pages.text: Kota loved the sound of wooden clogs. Clack, clack across the yard! Excited, Kota climbed onto the porch. BANG! The whole house shook.
A crane napping inside opened his door. "I thought that was thunder!" Kota looked down at their feet. "Thunder?"
Kota's shoulders drooped. "I love that clacking sound. Can't I make it anymore?" They fiddled with the toe of a clog.
Dad came into the yard. "Clogs are instruments for the yard. Shall we play them?" Kota's eyes grew round.
On the dirt, Kota took little clacking steps. On the stepping stones—TAK! TAK! Every place made a different sound.
At the porch, Kota slipped off the clogs and lined them up. Bare paws padded softly inside. "I'll leave my instruments in the yard."
A yard concert began. The crane woke and nodded along on the porch. "What a wonderful performance!" Kota's tail stood tall.
The crane tapped his beak on the porch. Tok, tok, tok! "Here's my drum!" The yard filled with cheerful sounds.
One, take the clogs off. Two, place them side by side. Three, clack away in the yard! Quiet inside, music outside.
Dad, barefoot too, gathered Kota onto his lap. A happy sound in the right place became a song. "Clack, clack, in the yard!" Kota wiggled their toes and laughed.
